message.content:
Below is everything you’ll need to post your “Confirmed #malware” comment to **VirusTotal** for the IP `192.168.1.1`.  
(Keep in mind that `192.168.x.x` is a *private* address block – unless you’re running a local VT instance, VirusTotal won’t find anything there.)

---

### 1️⃣ What’s required

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Endpoint | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` |
| Method | `POST` |
| Headers | `x-apikey`, `Content-Type: application/json` |
| Body | Your supplied JSON |

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type":"comments",
    "attributes":{
      "text":"Confirmed #malware"
    }
  }
}
```

> ⚠️ Notice the wrapper around `"data"`—the V3 API expects the top‑level object to contain a `"data"` field.  

---

### 2️⃣ Quick ways to hit the API

#### A) Using **curl**

```bash
curl -X POST \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data-binary @-
```
After pressing Enter once, paste the body from above and press Ctrl+D (or just type `EOF`).  
Example full command:

```bash
cat <<EOF | curl -X POST \
   https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments \
   -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
   -H "Accept: application/json" \
   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   --data-binary @-

{"data":{"type":"comments","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}}

EOF
```

#### B) Using **Python (`requests`)**

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustooltip.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"

payload = {
    "data": {
        "type": "comments",
        "attributes": {
            "text": "Confirmed #malware"
        }
    }
}

headers = {
    "x-apikey": "ABC321",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)

print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.json())
```

Replace `abc321` with your actual key and run the script. If the IP isn’t indexed yet, you’ll receive a `404 Not Found`; otherwise you’ll see a success status (`201 Created`) along with the newly created comment ID.

---

### 3️⃣ Things to double‑check

| Check | Why |
|-------|-----|
| **Public vs. private IP** | VirusTotal indexes only publicly routable IPs. `192.168.*` will return “not found.” |
| **Key safety** | Never expose your API key in shared scripts or version control. Store it in environment variables or secret managers. |
| **Rate limits** | VT allows ~4–5 requests per minute for free accounts. Exceeding triggers throttling. |
| **Comment length & formatting** | Keep text concise (<2000 chars); avoid personal info. |

---

### 4️⃣ Troubleshooting quick tips

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `401 Unauthorized` | Wrong/missing key | Verify header spelling and value. |
| `403 Forbidden` | Key lacks permission | Upgrade plan or contact support. |
| `400 Bad Request` | Malformed JSON | Ensure proper quoting and structure. |
| `404 Not Found` | IP not present | Confirm IP is public and already scanned. |

That’s all! Once you fire off one of those commands, the comment should stick (assuming the IP is indexable). Happy scanning!
